title: Source register
description: Every factual claim in this repository traces to a row here. Verification level is recorded honestly: FETCHED means the page was opened and read in this session; INDEX-MEANS means the text was seen only through a search index of the official document (the document itself was not opened at page level); LINKED means the URL was reached from an official page but was not opened; UNREACHABLE means we tried and it failed (kept, because a dead official path is itself a finding).

rows.claim: The NFL publishes one league-wide Official Injury Report per game, grouped by matchup, with columns Player / Position / Injuries / Practice Status / Game Status, updated on each practice day of the game week (Week 10 2026 shows a Thursday, Nov 12 report for Sunday, Nov 15 games and a Tuesday, Nov 10 report for the Thursday game).
rows.note: Page title read: 'Official Latest NFL Injury Report for Players - Week 10 of the 2026 Season'. Season selector runs 1965-2026 and a week selector runs Week 1-10 in this view, which is what makes a historical availability archive technically possible. Only chunk 1 of 8 was captured, so our snapshot is a partial sample, never the full report. Capture protocol proven in-session: two fetches of this URL ~1 hour apart returned 24 and 68 rows for the same six club tables with zero contradictions, so 'the report' is only meaningful as 'the report as rendered at timestamp T' — data/injury_snapshot.json (A) and data/injury_snapshot_b.json (B) are both committed to demonstrate it.

rows.claim: Competition Committee revisions to the Injury Report Policy: Practice Report uses Did Not Participate / Limited Participation (<100% of normal reps) / Full Participation (100% of normal reps); Game Status Report dropped 'Probable' (about 95% of Probable players had played) and defines Questionable = uncertain, Doubtful = unlikely, Out = will not play; a player certain to play is not listed in the Game Status Report, and if he is then deactivated the club must explain to the league and may be disciplined.
rows.note: Content is the official NFL.com release quoted verbatim in the search result body for this exact URL. Critical consequence for us: the official definitions are qualitative. No official percentage is attached to 'Questionable' or 'Doubtful', so any P(play) number we use must be estimated from data, not quoted as league policy.

rows.claim: Roster architecture that determines who replaces a starter: 53-man Active/Inactive list; 54/55 only via practice-squad elevation; practice squad of 16; Reserve/Injured carries a minimum four-game absence with up to eight 'designated to return' per team (each player twice); Reserve/PUP and Reserve/NFI also clear after four games; Reserve/Suspended, Retired, Did Not Report, Military and Commissioner Exempt do not count against roster limits.
rows.publisher: NFL.com — league official news (Ian Hartitz roster FAQs)
rows.note: FLAG: the article is written around the 2022 league year (it still discusses suspended COVID protocols and cites 2022 amendments). The four-game IR minimum and eight designations should be re-confirmed against the current CBA / 2026 rulebook before they are coded as constants. Treated here as 'as-described 2022' rather than current law.

rows.claim: NFL Football Operations is the league's own hub for rules and policies (homepage carries '2026 NFL RULEBOOK'), the official Important Dates calendar, and announces league analytics competitions (Big Data Bowl, powered by AWS).
rows.note: Also confirms two operational dates relevant to model timing ('Player Signing Deadline 4:00 pm ET' on Nov 17; 'Special League Meeting' Dec 9 virtual) and that https://operations.nfl.com/the-rules is NOT a valid path (returns the NFL 404 'Flag on the play' page) — so our rules-citation URL must be rebuilt from the live navigation.

rows.claim: Official contract-language reference: gameday roster is 47 or 48 players; the active/inactive list is 53 in regular season and playoffs; a team may reach 54 or 55 only by elevating one or two practice-squad players under the Standard Elevation Addendum; each practice-squad player may be elevated a maximum of three games per league year; practice-squad eligibility was amended in May 2022.
rows.note: The 47/48 active-inactive split is the mechanical reason 'one fewer starter' can become 'two fewer players on the bus' for special teams; it is directly usable by our availability model.

rows.claim: The league calendar of operational deadlines (roster cutdowns, signing deadlines, league meetings) is published on one official page and is machine-scrapable by anchor (e.g. #nov-17).
rows.note: Reached from SRC-004's rendered navigation; not opened in this pass. Needed to fix our transaction-freeze dates (a Wednesday 4pm deadline changes what Friday's report can contain).

rows.claim: Ahead of the 2026 season the NFL signed multi-year deals with DraftKings, FanDuel and Fanatics Betting and Gaming; all three agreed to league integrity policies, including working together to prohibit wagers tied to officiating and injuries and bets that can be knowable in advance or easily manipulated by a single person; official data flows through Genius Sports as exclusive distributor; the league runs responsible-gambling programmes with NCPG ($6.2M in 2021, $6.4M in 2024).
rows.publisher: NFL.com — league official press release (27 Aug 2026)
rows.note: Opened in full. Two hard planning consequences: (1) official real-time play-by-play, Next Gen Stats and the official betting feed are only available through one licensed distributor, so 'just scrape it' is not a compliant architecture; (2) injury-linked markets are ones the league asks operators not to offer, which shapes what our signals may be attached to.

rows.claim: The NFL's own published framework for legalized sports betting: prohibited wager classes are (a) Inherently Objectionable (e.g. player injuries, fan safety, misconduct), (b) Officiating-Related (assignments, penalties, replays), (c) Determinable by One Person in One Play (e.g. kicker to miss, QB's first pass incomplete), (d) Pre-Determined outcomes (e.g. 'Will QB start this week?'). Prediction markets on games are treated as sports betting. Each club has an assigned Integrity Representative, Genius Sports monitors betting patterns in real time, the Global Security Operations Center monitors insider threats, and all players/coaches/staff must sign and train on the Gambling Policy annually, which bans betting on the NFL, betting at team facilities/hotels, entering a sportsbook in season, playing daily fantasy football and sharing inside information.
rows.publisher: media.nfl.com — league official (Legalized Sports Betting hub)
rows.note: Opened and read (chunk 1 of 2). This is the compliance gate for the entire project: it is the list we hard-exclude from both our market universe and our feature engineering.

rows.claim: NFL.com maintains an official directory of all 32 clubs, each with a league-hosted team profile and a link to the club's own site.
rows.note: Used to establish where roster/depth material is officially hosted. FLAG: https://www.nfl.com/teams/transactions redirects to /teams/ in this session, and https://www.nfl.com/teams/new-england-patriots/depth-chart returns the NFL 404 page — so there is currently no verified league-level depth-chart or transactions endpoint. Depth charts must come from club sites (also official, but club-operated), which changes our per-team scraping contract.

rows.claim: The Illinois Gaming Board publishes Monthly Sports Wagering Reports with a matching CSV, selectable by report type (All Wagering Activity / Completed Events; Detail Report; Sport Detail Report; Tax Summary) and by month range back to March 2020, and states that revenue is not due until the last day of the month after it is earned.
rows.note: Opened. 'Sport Detail Report' is the field we need: it is an official, free, machine-readable series that lets us sanity-check hold by sport and by market family instead of trusting industry folklore. Publication lag (~1 month) is a constraint on any live feature that claims to be calibrated to current hold.

rows.claim: The New York State Gaming Commission publishes Statewide and per-operator Sports Wagering reports in both PDF and Excel, monthly and weekly.
rows.note: FLAG: seen through a search-index render of the official page (which listed Caesars Sport Book and DraftKings Sport Book, dated Oct 2024). Weekly + Excel granularity is the single most useful public regulatory dataset for market-microstructure work, but the operator list and current cadence must be re-opened before we cite any number from it.

rows.claim: Nevada's Minimum Internal Control Standards for Race and Sports require each book to keep monthly and year-to-date reports of total wagers accepted, total paid, taxable win and win-to-write percentage for each sport AND for sports parlay cards separately, to trace 5% of events daily against an independent source, and to have those reports reviewed quarterly under Regulation 22.040.
rows.note: Paragraphs 78, 81, 105, 106 quoted from the search index of the official MICRS PDF; document not opened at page level. Relevance: parlay hold is audited as its own category, which is the regulator's own admission that parlay pricing behaves unlike straight wagers — the premise of our correlation section.

rows.claim: Nevada's Monthly Revenue Report carries a per-category table (Race Book, Sports Pool) with win amount, win percent and month/YTD/annual columns, and its published tables may not foot because of rounding; a sports-handle figure is not directly published and is derived by dividing win by win percent.
rows.note: FLAG: two of our guessed landing paths (gaming.nv.gov/gaming-activities/gaming-revenue-reports and /about/gaming-revenue) returned 404; only the direct PDF path is evidenced, via a search index that showed June-2026 rows. Therefore NO Nevada number is published in this repository as verified. Specific hold percentages (e.g. the widely quoted 'parlay cards ~38%') remain UNVERIFIED and are quarantined on the Flagged page until the PDF is opened.

rows.claim: Approved operator house rules (DraftKings, as filed with a state regulator): a parlay other than a Same Game Parlay 'shall never include two or more offers where the outcomes of which might turn out to be related', and if related outcomes slip through the operator may void the affected legs; a Same Game Parlay with a void or push leg is repriced from the odds available at the time of bet placement; a SGP has action only if the game starts within 24 hours of the original start time and in the originally scheduled week, which for the NFL is Thursday-Wednesday in local stadium time.
rows.publisher: massgaming.com — state regulator hosting operator house rules (official for that operator in MA)
rows.note: Read from the search index of the regulator-hosted PDF (also mirrored at a licensed casino's own site). This is the primary source for our rule 'never assume a correlated parlay will settle as the product of its legs'. Version-stamped 2024-08-01; re-check before coding settlement logic.

rows.claim: Peer-reviewed evidence that NFL betting markets remain statistically inefficient: sportsbooks under-estimate home teams (especially home underdogs that failed to cover their previous game), and totals show a quadratic relationship to the closing line plus a streak effect after the home team covered the Over. Break-even at -110 is stated as 52.38% ($110 / $210).
rows.publisher: Journal of Economics and Finance 42:818-827 (2018), Springer — academic
rows.note: Abstract, notes and reference list read (paywalled body not available). Its reference apparatus is the anchor for the whole literature layer below: Borghesi (2007) J Econ Bus 59:340-354; Camerer (1989) Am Econ Rev 79:1257-1261; Brown & Sauer (1993) Am Econ Rev 83:1377-1386; Dare & Holland (2004) Applied Econ 36:9-15; Dare & MacDonald (1996) J Fin Econ 40:295-318; DiFilippo et al. (2014) J Sports Econ 15:201-211; Paul & Weinbach (2005) J Sports Econ 6:390-400; Amoako-Adu et al. (1985) J Econ Bus 37:365-378; Levitt (2004) Econ J 114:223-246 — each verified only as a citation string on this fetched page, not in the original.

rows.claim: The statistical machinery for removing luck from a strategy leaderboard: White's Reality Check (Econometrica 68(5):1097-1126, doi:10.1111/14680262.00152), Hansen's Superior Predictive Ability test (J Bus Econ Stat 23(4):365-380, doi:10.1198/073500105000000063), Romano & Wolf's stepwise extension, the deflated Sharpe ratio (Bailey & Lopez de Prado 2014), and the Ledoit-Wolf paired stationary bootstrap; plus the data-snooping lineage (Lo & MacKinlay 1990; Brock, Lakonishok & LeBaron 1992; Sullivan, Timmermann & White 1999).
rows.note: Citation strings with volume, pages and DOIs taken from the search index of the CRAN PDF. Sufficient to specify the gates and to name the tests we will implement; re-open before quoting any test's assumptions in a paper our own reviewers will read.

rows.claim: NFL money-line markets (2007-2016) show measurable inefficiency in both openers and closers, a reverse favorite-longshot bias (bettors overbet the favourite, underbet the dog), that the inefficiency is unpredictable and varies by season, and that precipitation creates a betting-favourite profit opportunity.
rows.publisher: Journal of Economic Insight 50(2), published 2024-12-31 — academic
rows.note: Abstract read via search index of the journal's own article page. Used only as a prior that 'the closing line is not the truth'; never as a staking rule.

rows.claim: The NFL season win-total market is 'highly inefficient' largely because bettors over-react to a team's previous-season record and fail to regress it to the mean (representativeness heuristic).
rows.note: Hosted on a third-party repository; DOI and journal shown in the indexed abstract. Motivation for our shrinkage priors, not evidence about spreads.

rows.claim: Kelly's original result: for a binary bet at fair odds the optimal growth fraction equals the information rate of the signal, generalised to arbitrary odds; Kelly, Bell System Technical Journal 35(4):917-926 (1956).
rows.publisher: Bell System Technical Journal (1956) — academic, primary
rows.note: FLAG: the bibliographic record (author, journal, volume, issue, pages, year) was cross-checked in three independent reference lists, but no canonical publisher URL was confirmed in this session and the guessed domain does not exist. We therefore cite the citation, not a link. Do not present a URL to this paper until a real one is opened. Note also that the Kelly fraction maximises log-growth, not the probability of not going broke — our staking spec uses fractional Kelly for that reason.

rows.claim: Genius Sports is the NFL's exclusive distributor of real-time official play-by-play statistics, Next Gen Stats and the official sports betting data feed to media companies and betting operators, extended on 11 June 2025 through the end of the 2029 season, including BetVision.
rows.publisher: Genius Sports investor relations — licensor official
rows.note: Corroborated independently by the league's own release (SRC-007), which is why we treat the exclusivity fact as solid even though this page was read via index. It is the reason the data-acquisition plan is a purchase decision, not a scraping decision.

rows.claim: Clubs publish their own formatted injury reports alongside the league file, including 'Not Injury Related - Resting Player' rows and change-marking conventions (bold indicates change in status), and their reports state that participation is an estimation.
rows.note: Indexed extract of a club-hosted report for Buccaneers at Patriots, 3 Oct 2021, showing the legend FP/LP/DNP, Out/Doubtful/Questionable and 'Bold indicates change in status'. Establishes two things we need: rest days are on the report and must be filtered out of injury signals, and status *changes* (not levels) are the tradeable event.

rows.claim: Independent reporting on the Week 10 2026 NFL gambling landscape and current club availability practice used only for cross-checking context, never as a source of rules or numbers in our tables.
rows.publisher: Secondary sports media (The Athletic, CBS Sports, SI, Covers, Marca)
rows.note: Kept on the register deliberately to mark the boundary: material from this class may appear in prose as 'reported', but no table row depends on it. Ten players suspended for gambling violations in 2023 and 25 team/league employees disciplined that season are examples of enforcement, and are not needed for any decision here.

rows.claim: Gambling-helpline resources that must sit in the site footer: the National Council on Problem Gambling helpline (1-800-GAMBLER) is the referral point state regulators link to, alongside state-specific help pages.
rows.publisher: ncpgambling.org via igb.illinois.gov footer — non-profit, regulator-endorsed
rows.note: Reached from the Illinois Gaming Board's own responsible-gambling footer (SRC-010). Not opened in this pass; opening it is a task, not an assumption. Included because a project that helps someone stake money without a help link is a project with a foreseeable harm.

rows.claim: The repository as delivered by its owner contains no data, schema, code or configuration: one tracked file, README.md, six bytes, text '# FL1', on a single commit.
rows.note: Verified twice, in two independent ways: locally with git (`git ls-tree -r HEAD`, `git log`, byte count) and against the hosted repository with `gh api repos/sassnix321/FL1/commits/e001e0a...`, which returns the same sha with message 'Initial commit' and author sassnix321-star. This is the audit finding the brief asked for: there is nothing in the repo to verify, so every number in this project must be sourced from the registers above or left blank. The URL is a permalink to the commit, not to a branch head, so it cannot drift.
